source_text: Igitur, quoniam filii Israel affirmant nos errare recipiendo Christum, qui jam venit, praescribamus eis ex ipsis Scripturis jam venisse Christum qui praedicabatur; quamvis ex temporibus Danielis praedicantis probaverimus jam venisse Christum, qui nuntiabatur. Nasci enim eum oportuit in Bethlehem Judae; sic enim scriptum est in propheta: Et tu Bethlehem, non minima es in ducibus Juda: ex te enim exiet dux qui pascat populum meum Israel. Si autem adhuc natus non est qui processurus dux de tribu Juda ex Bethlehem nuntiabatur, oportet enim eum de tribu Juda et a Bethlehem procedere; animadvertimus autem nunc neminem de genere Israel in civitate Bethlehem remansisse, et exinde quod interdictum est ne in confinio ipsius regionis demoretur quisquam Judaeorum, ut hoc quoque esset adimpletum per prophetam: Terra vestra deserta, civitates vestrae igni exustae, id est quod belli tempore eis evenerit; regionem vestram in conspectu vestro exteri comedent, et deserta et subversa erit a populis alienis. Et alio loco sic per prophetam dicitur: Regem cum claritate videbitis, id est Christum facientem virtutes in gloria Dei patris, et oculi vestri videbunt terram de longinquo: quod vobis pro meritis vestris post expugnationem Hierusalem, prohibitis ingredi in terram vestram, de longinquo eam oculis tantum videre permissum est. Anima, inquit, vestra meditabitur timorem. scilicet quo tempore excidium sui passi sunt. Quomodo igitur nascetur dux de Judaea, et quatenus procedet de Bethlehem, sicut divina prophetarum volumina nuntiant, cum nullus omnino sit illic in hodiernum derelictus ex Israel, cujus ex stirpe possit nasci Christus? Si enim, secundum Judaeos, adhuc non venit, cum venire coeperit, unde ungetur? Lex enim praecepit, in captivitate non licere unctionem chrismatis regalis confici. Si autem jam nec unctio est illis, ut Daniel prophetavit; dicit enim: Exterminabitur unctio: ergo jam non est illic unctio, quia nec templum ubi erat cornu de quo reges ungebantur. Si ergo non est unctio, unde ungetur dux qui nascetur in Bethlehem? aut quomodo procedet de Bethlehem, cum de germine Israel nullus omnino sit in Bethlehem?
thought_title: Christ's Birthplace and the Jewish People
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, since the sons of Israel affirm that we are mistaken in receiving Christ, who has already come, let us prescribe to them from their own Scriptures that Christ, who was being preached, has already come; although we have proven from the times of Daniel, who was preaching, that Christ, who was being announced, has already come. For He was born in Bethlehem of Judah; thus it is written in the prophet: And you, Bethlehem, are not the least among the leaders of Judah: for from you will come a leader who will pasture my people Israel. But if He has not yet been born, who was announced as the leader to come from the tribe of Judah and from Bethlehem, it is necessary for Him to come from the tribe of Judah and from Bethlehem; we notice, however, that now no one from the race of Israel remains in the city of Bethlehem, and from this it is also forbidden that any Jew may dwell in the border of that region, so that this also may be fulfilled through the prophet: Your land will be deserted, your cities will be burned with fire, that is, what happened to them in time of war; your region will be eaten by foreigners in your sight, and it will be deserted and overturned by alien peoples. And in another place it is said through the prophet: You will see the King with glory, that is, Christ performing mighty deeds in the glory of God the Father, and your eyes will see the land from afar: because you, according to your merits, after the capture of Jerusalem, were forbidden to enter your land, it was permitted for you to see it only with your eyes from afar. Your soul, it says, will meditate on fear, namely at the time when they suffered their own destruction. How, therefore, will the leader be born from Judah, and how will He come from Bethlehem, as the divine volumes of the prophets announce, when there is no one at all left there today from Israel, from whose stock Christ can be born? For if, according to the Jews, He has not yet come, when He begins to come, from where will He be anointed? For the law commanded that the anointing of the royal chrism is not permitted in captivity. But if there is no anointing for them now, as Daniel prophesied; for he says: The anointing will be destroyed: therefore, there is no anointing there now, because there is no temple where the horn was, from which the kings were anointed. If, therefore, there is no anointing, from where will the leader who will be born in Bethlehem be anointed? Or how will He come from Bethlehem, when there is no one at all from the seed of Israel in Bethlehem?

pass_b_english: Since the sons of Israel insist we are wrong to accept Christ, who has already come, let us prove from their own Scriptures that the promised Christ has indeed arrived—even though the chronology of Daniel's prophecy already makes this clear. He had to be born in Bethlehem of Judah, for the prophet writes: "And you, Bethlehem, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel" (Micah 5:2). If that ruler has not yet been born, he still must arise from the tribe of Judah and from Bethlehem; yet today not a single descendant of Israel remains in Bethlehem, and Jews are forbidden even to dwell in its surrounding territory—fulfilling the prophet's words: "Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire"—that is, what befell them in wartime; "your land is devoured by foreigners before your eyes, desolate and overthrown by alien peoples." Elsewhere the prophet declares: "You will see the King in his beauty"—meaning Christ working mighty deeds in the glory of God the Father—"and your eyes will see the land from afar" (cf. Daniel 9:26): because of your merits, after Jerusalem's capture you were barred from entering your land, permitted only to gaze on it from a distance. "Your soul will meditate on terror"—that is, at the moment they suffered their own destruction. So how can the ruler be born from Judah and come forth from Bethlehem, as the divine prophetic scrolls announce, when no Israelite stock remains there today from which Christ could spring? If, as the Jews claim, he has not yet come, then when he does begin to come, from where will he be anointed? The law forbade the preparation of royal chrism in captivity. And if there is now no anointing for them, as Daniel foretold—"The anointing shall be cut off"—then no anointing exists, because the temple is gone, along with the horn from which kings were anointed. If there is no anointing, how will the ruler born in Bethlehem be anointed? Or how will he proceed from Bethlehem when not a single descendant of Israel remains there?

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version with appropriate scripture citations (Micah 5:2 and Daniel 9:26) which were alluded to in the Latin. The citations in Pass B correctly identify the source of the quoted prophetic text.
